notes:
Typescript headed “Compléments sur transformation de Coxeter d'un système de racines”, with a circled handwritten irreducibility qualification and “(Kostant)”. The handwritten English reference reads “The principal 3-dimensional subgroup .... th. 9.2.” No author date or document page count appears; the archival sheet number is 1 (comment only).

Statement a) bounds the orders of eigenvalues in terms of the characteristic exponents and identifies the case of a primitive h-th root with a Coxeter transformation and regular eigenvectors. The first corollary identifies the centralizer of a Coxeter element with its cyclic subgroup mu, and describes the quotient of its normalizer by mu through Aut(mu). A margin asks, “Quelle extension de (Z/hZ]* par Z/hZ obtient-on ?”; the squared closing delimiter and the placement of par are preserved, with local alphabet uncertainty. Another note requests “échanger avec cor.3”, with the word ending still doubtful.

The centralizer proof is internally valid conditional on its stated inputs: a finite cyclic scalar image contains mu, its generator has eigenvalue order at most h, and the kernel fixes a regular vector. The elementary order and kernel deductions were checked; Kostant's assertions, the prop.30 citation, and the regular-vector stabilizer premise were not proved here. The source says “il faut prouver que son noyau est réduit à 1” and immediately supplies that argument; “Reste à prouver” introduces the conjugacy assertion, which it attributes to Kostant. These are the source's proof transitions, not new claims of independent verification.

The formula wcw^{-1}=c^h is a visible typed slip: the crop shows a tall h, although c^h=1 cannot be conjugate to an element of order h>1. The later c^n is recorded as a separate assertion, never substituted into the transcription. In the following corollary the h′ exponent is visibly a prime. The necessity argument was checked conditionally: h divides h′ and 1<=h′<=h, so h′=h. The literal “conjugué de c” and “droite régulières” are retained. The bottom corollary continues onto another sheet after “élé”; its three overwritten/canceled opening layers are transcribed separately. Detailed check types and limits are in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

Two marks omitted by both witnesses are retained with doubt: the covered baseline i beneath the raised f in effet, and the detached point before the first c^{h′}. The latter has no secure mathematical role; the transcription does not turn it into an inferred operation. The number of faint dot leaders in the English annotation remains uncertain (four or three). The centralizer symbol has a typed z-shaped upper part plus a handwritten lower loop; its first occurrence records the Fraktur/plain alternatives. The upper handwritten Z pair in the margin is uncertain, while the lower pair has distinct doubled diagonals.

The numeral 30 is read identically by all readers, but its production differs in their reports. The main reader favors the thin drawn contours and retains C’s handwritten marking, with medium confidence; this is recorded as a reader-only origin disagreement, not counted as a changed word or symbol.
Pre-freeze notation comparison resolves the bottom product mark as the visible typewriter oval-plus-serifed-x construction, matching both occurrences on 123/018. The earlier tensor-sign alternative concerned interpretation, not unreadable physical strokes, and is therefore removed from the in-place doubt.
